questions.q: What genuinely new capability did Genie Code gain at Data + AI Summit 2026 for managing longer-running work?
options: A full-page command center for managing multiple concurrent threads scoped to different notebooks or assets, replacing the small side panel for complex work
The ability to write SQL for the first time, which it previously could not do
Removal of all human review before changes are applied
A requirement that every task be scheduled, with interactive use removed entirely
questions.explain: The redesigned full-page command center lets users manage multiple concurrent threads, track progress, and review outputs, instead of being confined to a small side panel.

questions.q: What are Genie Code's two distinct sources of expertise, per this lesson?
options: Databricks' own decade-plus of production ML experience, and the team's own Genie Ontology (how that specific team builds features, trains models, and evaluates candidates)
Only generic internet-scraped coding examples, with no team-specific knowledge at all
Exclusively the user's own prompts, with no platform-level knowledge involved
A single static rulebook that never updates across customers
questions.explain: Genie Code applies lessons learned from Databricks' own production ML experience, and closes the team-specific gap through Genie Ontology, which learns a given team's actual patterns.

questions.q: What are the four steps of Genie ZeroOps's process for handling a detected failure, in order?
options: Detect, Assess, Remediate, Verify
Verify, Remediate, Assess, Detect
Detect, Remediate, Verify, Assess
Only two steps exist: Detect and Fix
questions.explain: ZeroOps runs Detect (continuous monitoring, including silent failures), Assess (root cause via Unity Catalog lineage), Remediate (agentic code generation), then Verify (sandboxed testing against real data before any human approval).

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a generic external coding agent specifically cannot safely perform the Verify step?
options: Verification requires testing a fix against real production data in an isolated environment, and production data can't be freely handed to an external tool without either denying access or risking real side effects
Generic coding agents are incapable of writing any code that resembles a fix
Verification is purely a licensing restriction with no technical basis
Generic agents can verify fixes perfectly well; this is not actually a real distinction
questions.explain: Production data is sensitive and governed — an external agent either can't get safe access to it, or if it did, could cause real side effects testing against it. ZeroOps solves this by running inside the platform with zero-copy clones and isolation.

questions.q: For an ML model fix specifically, what does ZeroOps evaluate the corrected candidate against before surfacing it?
options: The same eval suite and criteria the production model was originally held to, not a generic benchmark, surfacing the candidate only if it's measurably better
A randomly chosen industry-standard benchmark unrelated to the original model
No evaluation at all — candidates are applied directly to production traffic immediately
Only the training loss value, ignoring any business evaluation criteria
questions.explain: ZeroOps evaluates a corrected ML candidate against the exact eval suite and criteria the production model was originally held to, and only surfaces it if it's measurably better, letting the human ramp it onto live traffic gradually.
